open_obligations: Check that a stochastic oracle with constant advantage over random guessing is an adequate model of human error.
Note the authors themselves leave oracles with systematic errors on some queries open.
Check whether the efficient-honest-prover requirement changes the class of decidable problems relative to PSPACE.
in.other_title: Theorem 6.2: stochastic-oracle doubly-efficient debate with O(K^2) human queries
in.rationale: Irving et al. note their theory models judges as error-free and agents as unbounded and call for richer models. Brown-Cohen et al. require the honest prover to run in polynomial time and, in Theorem 6.2, allow a stochastic human-judgement oracle (K-Lipschitz machine, O(K^2) queries, completeness 3/5, soundness 2/5), which relaxes both assumptions partially; the dishonest prover is still unbounded and the oracle is not allowed arbitrary errors.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate theory can drop the error-free judge and unbounded debaters of the DEBATE = PSPACE analogy, for oracle machines with a stochastic human-judgement oracle

open_obligations: Check that the expertise gap (hidden passage) is a fair stand-in for the capability gap Irving et al. target.
Note that debaters were not trained toward equilibrium, so the result is about judge usability, not equilibrium behaviour.
Check the 92.5% estimated upper bound and how it was computed before reading the 84% as near-ceiling.
in.other_title: Debate beats consultancy for non-expert human judges: 84% vs 74% on hard QuALITY questions
in.rationale: Irving et al. state debate had only an MNIST demonstration and that significant research is needed to know whether it works with human judges. Michael et al. report human-debater debates judged by non-expert humans reach 84% accuracy versus 74% for consultancy on QuALITY-hard; the debaters are humans or GPT-4, not agents trained by self-play.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate works in practice with human judges in natural language, on QuALITY-hard hidden-passage questions

text: The authors state that debate is at this point a proposal only for the natural-language case, that only a basic MNIST experiment has been demonstrated, and that significant research is required to know whether debate works in practice with human judges. They note that their DEBATE = PSPACE discussion models judges as limited but free of error and agents as having unlimited computational power, and call for richer theoretical models.
title: Debate is a proposal only for natural language; theory assumes error-free judges
